title: A Guide to Build a Highly Inclined Swept Tile Microscope for Extended Field-of-view Single-molecule Imaging
protocol: Set up the microscope, lasers, and alignment tools as described.
Prepare all necessary components including optics, optomechanics, and electronics.
Construct the microscope body consisting of an objective holder with an RMS-threaded port.
Mount a piezo-stage on an aluminum block to complete the microscope body.
Install 405 nm, 561 nm, and 638 nm lasers onto the optical table.
Combine laser beams through a polarizing beam splitter and long-pass dichroic mirror.
Ensure all laser beams pass through pinholes on the alignment tool.
Insert half wave plates for power adjustment of each laser.
Install a fiber coupling lens (f = 4.5 mm).
Use a fiber adapter held in z-axis translator with a cage system.
Connect a multimode fiber (Ø 62.5 µm) to the fiber adapter.
Adjust each steering mirror and z-translator pair until coupling efficiency exceeds 95% for all lasers.
Take away the multimode fiber.
Connect a single mode fiber (SMF).
Fine-tune and maximize the coupling efficiency of three lasers using SMF.
Assemble a collimated light source composed of a temporally coherent light source (561 nm) connected to SMF, fiber adapter, achromatic lens (f = 60 mm), iris, and Ø1" tube spacer in a cage system.
Adjust the distance between the fiber adapter and the lens using a shearing interferometer for collimation.
Prepare a beam alignment tool consisting of a pair of aluminum posts with pinholes at 2" height from the surface of optical table.
Assemble a double pinhole system with two Ø1" ground glass alignment disks at each end and two Ø1" lens tubes (the bottom one is slotted).
Take out the objective.
Install the collimated light source.
Adjust the knobs of mirror (M1) beneath the objective holder to align the output beam roughly parallel to the optical table in height.
Insert a multiband dichroic mirror (DM) and reflect the beam by 90 degrees.
Use the maximum size of the iris to ensure the beam passes through the center of the dichroic mirror without clipping.
Place an sCMOS camera into the beam path and use two mirrors (M2 and M3) to align the beam so it hits the center of the camera chip.
Insert a tube lens (TL; f = 300 mm) approximately 300 mm away from the camera.
Remove the collimated light source and adjust the distance between the tube lens and the camera until a pattern on the ceiling is clearly resolved by the camera.
Insert a multi-band pass filter (BF) before the tube lens for multi-color fluorescence imaging.
Reinstall the collimated light source on the objective holder.
Place a fold-mirror (M4) to redirect the beam output from the microscope by 70 degrees.
Adjust the knobs of the dichroic mirror and the fold-mirror iteratively until the beam passes through pinholes in the beam alignment tool.
Detach the collimated light source and install it on the table, pointing towards the microscope body.
Align the beam using a beam alignment tool and a double pinhole system.
Insert lens L4 with f = 400 mm and Ø = 2" to the optical path, approximately 400 mm away from the objective holder.
Adjust position of L4 along the optical axis until a perfect Airy disk pattern is formed on the ceiling.
Unscrew the objective and reinstall the collimated light source with an open iris.
Trace down the beam output from the microscope using a business card.
Mount mirror M5 at the place where the beam size is smallest, approximately 400 mm away from L4.
Install mirror M6 and reflect the beam by 90 degrees.
Adjust mirrors M5 and M6 iteratively with the beam alignment tool.
Insert lens L3 with f = 150 mm roughly 150 mm away from M5.
Use a shearing interferometer to ensure collimation of the output beam.
Temporarily take away L4 and trace down the beam to find the focal position of L3.
Place a single-axis galvo mirror at this point, which is the conjugated back focal plane (cBFP).
Supply 0 volts to the galvo mirror and rotate its holder by 90 degrees.
Place fold-mirror M7.
Properly place lens L2 with f = 100 mm in the same manner as step 3.6.
Remove the collimated light source from the object holder.
Install a collimation lens L1 (f = 100 mm), fiber adapter and iris.
Connect a single mode fiber to the adapter and send the beam through the imaging system.
Reinsert L4 and fine tune the system until a perfect Airy disk pattern appears on the ceiling.
Insert a cylindrical lens (CL1, f = 400 mm) after L1 to focus the beam along the x-axis.
Insert another cylindrical lens (CL2, f = 50 mm) into the beam path.
Use a shearing interferometer to ensure the output beam is collimated.
Prepare a 3D hydrogel sample by mixing 20 nm Crimson beads with a hydrogel solution.
Inject 50 μL of the mixed solution into a flow chamber.
After 10 min, place the 3D hydrogel sample onto the sample holder for imaging.
Turn on 638 nm laser and adjust the power to <1 mW for excitation.
Run the camera control software and select Internal in trigger mode.
Click Take video for free running mode.
Adjust the position of the camera so that the image is centered when 0 volts are applied to the galvo mirror.
Rotate the horizontal knob of mirror M5 to achieve inclined illumination.
Record the tile image.
Calculate the effective illumination width.
Prepare a data acquisition board connected with a terminal block.
Connect USER 1 BNC connector with P0.0 through an electrical wire.
Use USER 1 as a digital output for external triggering of sCMOS camera.
Connect analog output AO0 to galvo mirror driver.
Generate TTL pulse trains from P0.0 using custom-made software, setting period time = 400 ms and t_ON = 2 ms.
Check generated pulses from USER 1 BNC terminal with a digital oscilloscope.
Connect the BNC cable to the camera external trigger port.
Start sweeping a galvo mirror via the custom-made program.
Adjust Vmin to -500 mV.
Adjust Vmax to 500 mV for full FOV imaging.
Select External in trigger mode.
Select Down (Sequential) in LightScan Plus drop-down menu.
Set values to be 180 rows and 28 ms for window height and line exposure time control.
Slightly adjust Vmax and Vmin to obtain clearer images.
Switch on 3D stack ON in the custom-made program.
Specify the number of stacks.
Specify the step size.
